title: TopoLite-KD
summary: Lightweight topology-aware knowledge distillation for COVID-19 CT-slice classification.
problem: Research into compact imaging models needs transparent framing of methods and limitations.
solution: A topology-aware knowledge-distillation approach explores lightweight architectures, attention, and explainability methods.
architecture: Case-study context: Compact medical-imaging research needs a transparent account of representation, topology, distillation, and explainability without implying clinical deployment.
Compact representation: A lightweight convolutional path is used as the student-side foundation for experimentation. Components: PyTorch, depthwise-separable CNN, EfficientNet-B0.
Topology-aware learning: Coordinate attention and persistent-homology signals are explored as structural guidance during distillation. Components: Coordinate Attention, persistent homology, GUDHI.
Interpretability: Grad-CAM provides a visual explanation surface for research inspection rather than a clinical guarantee. Components: Grad-CAM.
The README describes a lightweight student path using depthwise-separable convolution and EfficientNet-B0 components.
Coordinate Attention and persistent-homology signals implemented with GUDHI are explored as structural guidance for knowledge distillation.
Grad-CAM provides a research visualization; the project also links to a Kaggle experiment notebook.
outcomes: Research prototype exploring topology-aware knowledge distillation for compact CT classification.
Framed the work as an academic research prototype with explicit limitations.
Kept the public story focused on method and reproducibility rather than medical outcome claims.
A research prototype explores topology-aware knowledge distillation for compact COVID-19 CT-slice classification.
